memory_update.text: SPSC should be tracked as an underfollowed retail-supply-chain platform candidate for private-label/value-channel complexity; key proof points are retailer network breadth, recurring revenue durability, supplier adoption, and switching-cost evidence.

SENEA is a direct small-cap private-label/value-channel food-manufacturing candidate with unusually clear channel-language evidence: supermarkets, mass merchandisers, limited-assortment stores, club stores, and dollar stores.

COLD is a second-order cold-chain and store-support infrastructure candidate; later layers should separate private-label/value grocery upside from broader cold-storage occupancy and food-production volume headwinds.

TreeHouse Foods would have been one of the cleanest public private-label food-manufacturing comps, but evidence indicates it was taken private and delisted in February 2026; use it as an industry comp, not as a current US-listed candidate.

SPSC should be tracked as a hidden retail operating-system candidate: its exposure is less about consumer demand directly and more about supplier onboarding, EDI, retail compliance, order visibility, and trading-partner switching costs.

ODC is a niche private-label/value-staples materials candidate via lightweight cat litter and absorbent mineral supply; verify customer concentration and private-label mix before promoting beyond Layer 1.

SXT belongs in a regulated-input watchlist for private-label food reformulation, but the private-label linkage is currently indirect and requires primary evidence from filings, segment commentary, and customer/use-case disclosures.

The direct public pure-play private-label food co-manufacturing bucket became thinner after TreeHouse Foods completed its take-private transaction on February 11, 2026; future searches should look for remaining listed co-manufacturers, packaging suppliers, and ingredient firms one step away from store-brand production.
SPSC should be tracked as a retail-network/EDI compliance chokepoint for private-label and value-channel supplier enablement rather than as generic SaaS.
SENEA is a direct underfollowed private-label/contract-packaged food capacity candidate; later layers must verify customer concentration, crop-cycle volatility, and private-label margin quality.
JBSS is a private-brand and contract-manufacturing snack supplier candidate; later layers should test whether retail/customer concentration creates hidden upside or margin compression risk.

TreeHouse Foods would have been a high-relevance private-label manufacturer, but appears no longer US-listed after a February 2026 take-private; exclude from public universe unless debt/private-comps research is needed.

THS is the cleanest direct reference candidate for private-label packaged food manufacturing capacity, but later layers must test execution, recall risk, retailer concentration, and margin conversion.

SPSC should be tracked as a second-order retailer-supplier compliance network candidate; the key thesis is not private-label manufacturing but retailer integration, supplier onboarding, compliance logic, and order/fulfillment data complexity.
SENEA is a low-attention vertically integrated affordable food processor with potential value-channel/private-label relevance; verify private-label mix and large-retailer dependence before promotion.

AVO maps to perishables logistics, ripening, custom packaging, and retailer specification fulfillment; treat as a hypothesis because commodity avocado price and sourcing risk may dominate the chokepoint signal.

Need next-pass search for US-listed packaging suppliers, food-safety/testing labs, cold-chain REITs/logistics, and off-price retail logistics vendors with explicit Walmart/Costco/Aldi/dollar-store/private-label exposure.

node: Private-label, value-channel, club, off-price, and discount retail enablers
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct-public-company universe around value-channel and private-label enablement. The strongest direct public exposure in this pass is not a branded CPG leader, but infrastructure around retailer-supplier integration, low-cost packaged-food capacity, and cold-chain/store-support logistics. One mega-cap reference customer is included only as a demand anchor; the discovery lane emphasizes underfollowed small/mid-cap enablers where retailer specifications, audits, logistics reliability, and customer integrations may matter more than brand advertising. Layer 1B expansion focused on scarce suppliers, infrastructure, regulated inputs, and capacity-constrained enablers behind private-label and value retail. The strongest underfollowed candidates found in this pass are not retailers themselves, but retailer/supplier network software, food-and-grocery distribution infrastructure, regulated ingredient inputs for reformulation, and niche private-label staple materials. TreeHouse Foods would have been a direct private-label co-manufacturing reference, but it completed a take-private transaction on February 11, 2026, so it is excluded from the US-listed candidate list and retained only as a coverage-gap signal. Expanded the node around private-label/value-channel enablement with one mega-cap customer anchor and three underfollowed public suppliers or infrastructure assets. The strongest underfollowed angles are: retail EDI/compliance plumbing, private-label canned/frozen food capacity, and private-brand/contract snack-nut processing.
